content:
Plan for Phase 69 (cockpit roadmap board) at docs/phases/cockpit-roadmap-board.md, commit 45317ad on branch phase-69-cockpit-roadmap-board.

Decisions to review:
1. One reading: roadmap.board(root) (file-only, read-only safe), served by `tagteam roadmap board [--json]` and GET /api/roadmap. Groups, first match wins: done (terminal) · in_progress (the current cycle's phase, or a status that starts with In progress / In review / ✅ Approved) · ready / blocked (ready_phases / blocked_phases with the active run's completed list, in topological order). Graph problems are shown with their lines, and then nothing offers Start.
2. A bug found while planning: launch._next_after() picks the next phase in DOCUMENT order, blind to dependencies. The Start card and the hub can offer a blocked phase (the 2026-09-20 trial's "proposed Phase 44"). launch_intent gains an optional `phase`; without it, the default is the first READY phase in topological order. _next_after is removed.
3. Start on any ready phase through the existing /api/start/launch path. Each ready row carries the intent launch_intent(phase=X) returns, and launch() recomputes for the named phase with the same command+observed match, so a phase that stopped being ready gets a 409. The plan-approved rule: with a plan approved but not implemented, only `start <phase> impl` is offered. The orphan-launch reconciliation recomputes for the row's own phase.
4. The Start card is removed. The quiet Needs-you line points at the Roadmap tab with the server's ready_count. A failed launch shows on its row.
5. Tab regroup Now · Roadmap · Rules · History · Usage, with existing panel IDs kept, old saved-tab names mapped, and Diff kept lazy inside History. Offered as a split (69b) if you prefer it reviewed separately.

Open questions: the behaviour change from dropping document order (criterion 1 pins it); the closed list of "declared in-progress" status words; the split.

Reviewed the Phase 69 plan at 45317ad against roadmap readiness, launch_intent/launch, and the existing cockpit busy-state guard. Dependency-aware default selection is appropriate; keeping the tab regroup in this phase is also reasonable. The declared-status list is acceptable as a display convention, subject to the explicit lifecycle cases below.

Please resolve two gaps before implementation:

1. [P2] Make grouping exhaustive and distinguish an ended cycle from work in progress (section 1). The proposed Done rule uses only terminal roadmap text, while ready_phases, blocked_phases and topological_queue all exclude state.roadmap.completed. Thus a previously completed-in-run phase whose roadmap still says Not started, and which is no longer the current phase, falls into NONE of the four groups. Conversely the current-phase rule includes any existing cycle unless the roadmap marks it terminal, so an aborted cycle is labelled in progress and excluded from the board's ready set. The new launch selection would then prevent restarting that phase, despite the existing launch state machine treating aborted cycles as non-blocking. Specify where completed-in-run and aborted phases belong, with provenance when completion comes from the run rather than the document. Require every parsed phase to appear exactly once, and pin cases with stale roadmap status: A completed in the active run while B is current; and a current aborted cycle whose dependencies are met. If restarting aborted work is intentionally restricted, provide an explicit reason/recovery action rather than silently stranding it in In progress.

2. [P2] Preserve the global no-Start-while-busy rule for ALL board rows (sections 2-3). The plan explicitly applies the headline/busy guard only to the current row's Start implementation action. The old Start card applies it to every launch: any inflight marker, a pending launch, or headline working/starting/launching suppresses Start. With multiple ready rows, a first launch can be pending while handoff-state still says no cycle or impl approved; launch_intent alone does not inspect that pending launch/turn slot, so the other ready rows could still advertise Start. Define a single board-wide launch availability guard using the existing server facts, applied to all ready and implementation controls, with a reason while busy. Keep endpoint slot/idempotency protection and add a regression with two ready choices: start A before a cycle is created, refresh the board, and verify that neither A nor B advertises another runnable Start while A is pending/running. Also cover an unrelated active lead conversation and the plan-to-implementation transition. A stale second request must not deliver a second lead turn.

Implementation guidance: keep the pure roadmap classification/readiness snapshot separate from enriching rows with launch intents, so board() calling launch_intent() does not recursively call board() to select from its ready group. Reuse that classifier for both callers. Preserve lock-free/file-only board reads, including the graph-error path.

No tests were run for this plan review. No arbiter interjections or advisory standing orders were present.

Both r1 findings are addressed in docs/phases/cockpit-roadmap-board.md @ 243ae32.

1. Exhaustive grouping. A pure roadmap.classify(phases, state, cycle_status, completed) is shared by board() and launch_intent(); they never call each other, so there is no recursion. First match wins:
- done: done_by "roadmap" (terminal status) or "run" (in the active run's completed list despite a stale document status, with that status shown).
- in_progress: current (a live cycle, or a plan approved and not yet implemented) · approved (impl approved, roadmap not yet terminal, awaiting merge) · declared (status starts with In progress / In review / ✅ Approved). A declared phase gets no Start and an explicit recovery: "change its status to start it again".
- ready / blocked: the rest. An ABORTED current cycle is not in progress: it lands here with a "last cycle aborted" note and can be started again, matching the launch state machine.
Invariant: each parsed phase appears exactly once (asserted, and pinned over every fixture). Criterion 9 covers: A completed in the run with a stale status while B is current; an aborted current cycle with met dependencies is ready and its intent is accepted; a declared phase gets the recovery text and no Start.

2. One board-wide launch guard. roadmap_payload = board() + launch {available, reason}, computed from the facts the old Start card used (in-flight marker including a lead conversation turn, a pending launch row, headline working/starting/launching). While it is false, NO Start is runnable anywhere (the ready rows and Start implementation); each shows the reason. The endpoint enforces it too: launch() gains an up-front refusal inside its claim lock. Another pending launch, or a held turn slot, gives 409 "another start is in progress" with no launch row created. Today a second, different Start would claim a row and then fail on the slot: no second turn, but a noisy failed row. Same-intent idempotency is unchanged. Criterion 10: start A (pending, no cycle yet) → the board offers no Start for A or B; a stale POST for B → 409, no row, no second lead turn; an unrelated lead turn → unavailable, with the reason; the 68a automatic plan→impl handoff → no Start implementation. Tested at the API level and in real Chromium.

Also per your guidance: board() stays file-only and lock-free, including on the graph-error path. Only the API's launch guard reads the /api/now facts. The tab regroup stays in this phase, as you agreed.

Approved the revised plan at 243ae32.

The exhaustive classifier now accounts for phases completed in the active run despite stale roadmap text, exposes that provenance, and gives aborted current cycles a restart path. Declared in-progress phases have an explicit recovery explanation. Sharing the pure classifier between the board and launch selection keeps readiness consistent without recursive enrichment.

The board-wide launch guard covers ready rows and Start implementation, including pending launches, unrelated lead conversations and the automatic plan-to-implementation transition. The endpoint's claim-lock check rejects a different pending launch before creating another row while preserving same-intent idempotency. The added API/browser acceptance cases pin the identified gaps.

Dependency-aware default selection and the tab regroup remain approved. During implementation, preserve existing orphan reconciliation and retry semantics when evaluating pending launch rows; the new guard should not turn abandoned historical rows into a permanent launch block.

No remaining blocking plan findings. Plan review only; no tests were run. No arbiter interjections or advisory standing orders were present.
